messages:
maya rao: heads up — multiple gitlab runners started failing deploy jobs to prod around 14:02 UTC. seeing 403 from Redwood API when trying to exchange the OIDC assertion for a short-lived CI token. stack trace: `permission_denied: impersonation window mismatch`. this started right after the SA key rotation we pushed earlier today. anyone seen this?

sanjay patel: copying logs pls. which job types are failing (deploy step only?) and are they long-running?

maya rao: deploy step only. job duration varies — some are ~3m, others 12-15m. error snippet from runner:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] deploy: exchange_cred failed: 403 
{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"impersonation window invalid or expired"}
```
we rotated the service account credentials + tightened impersonation TTL to 5m as part of https://internal/ops/rotations (PR 412). previously TTL was 30m.

alex chen: that rings a bell — if the runner requests a token at job start and then the runner's environment tries to refresh/refresh-token concurrently after a rotation, you can hit a race where the impersonation delegation record doesn't line up. GitLab runners with long matrix jobs are vulnerable.

sanjay patel: repro plan: 1) start a job that sleeps 10m; 2) trigger a SA rotation in the middle (simulate by revoking/rotating credential) 3) attempt token refresh from job. I can repro locally with a quick script.

sanjay patel: snippet i used to inspect the OIDC assertion and token exchange: 
```bash
# dump oidc token claims from gitlab runner env
echo $CI_JOB_JWT | base64 --decode | jq . 
# exchange for redwood token (debug)
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/oauth/token \
  -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange" \
  -d "subject_token=$CI_JOB_JWT" \
  -d "requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token" \
  -d "scope=deploy:write"
```
response shows `exp` ~ 5m from issue time and the `aud` matches `gitlab-runner`.

maya rao: so short TTL is definitely the culprit for >5m jobs. why did we change it to 5m? was it for tighter security for a subset of customers?

ops-oncall: we set the default impersonation_ttl to 5m yesterday to harden ephemeral credentials after a security review. we landed a migration note but missed warnings for long-running CI. apologies.

alex chen: mitigation options: 
- short term: revert TTL back to 30m for the CI service account namespace or whitelist projects that run long jobs.
- medium: update gitlab-runner config to perform refresh with backoff and to detect 401/403 and re-run exchange logic gracefully.
- long term: provide a small SDK helper/middleware `redwood-ci-refresh` that will preemptively refresh tokens at half-life and automatically re-exchange if impersonation metadata changed.

sanjay patel: for least-privilege followup — ensure the exchanged tokens only have `deploy:write` and `artifact:read` scopes. do not grant `project:admin`. also add a constraint in IAM binding YAML: 
```yaml
bindings:
  - role: roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
    members: ["serviceAccount:gitlab-ci-sa@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
    condition:
      title: "ci-only"
      expression: "request.auth.claims.sub.startsWith(\"gitlab-runner-\")"
```

maya rao: i pushed a quick hotfix — ops-oncall allowed the CI namespace an exception (TTL -> 30m) while we implement SDK fix. kicked off a new deploy, monitoring.

deploy-bot: deploy/redwood-services prod failed at 14:02:11 (previous run 13:50:02) — retrying...

maya rao: new run succeeded after the exception. thanks team. can we make the exception audit-only and add a rollback plan?

ops-oncall: yes — i'll schedule a rollback window and add an alert if >5% of CI runs hit `impersonation window invalid`. also adding a doc in ops playbooks: `ci-token-best-practices.md`.

alex chen: action items for tracking: 
- SANJAY: create a repro test harness and run against rotated TTLs (owner: sanjay)
- ALEX: prototype `redwood-ci-refresh` in a small repo and publish example for gitlab-runner and actions (owner: alex)
- OPS: add exception audit + alert, rollback window, update rotation runbook (owner: ops-oncall)
- MAYA: update affected repos to use lightweight per-job tokens and minimal scopes (owner: maya)

sanjay patel: created issue https://internal/issues/9876 with repro steps and logs. attaching my local script and results.

maya rao: closing here — deploys green, will follow up if we see regressions. thanks :thumbsup:

support-bot: thread marked resolved by maya rao at 2026-03-15T14:18:13Z
